The mean 1 is physically attainable, while the second column of XSV^T is identically zero and the momentum is always zero. The replacement requires w0 nonzero and nonnegative; b>0 then implies positive mass, and normalization proves w0 is outside W if its target mean was missing. For the main theorem, the weighted marginals Fb and F^Ta are nonzero in their respective factor spaces; conversely the normalized product gives the target mass and momentum and exact rank one. Normalizing the spatial marginal gives the two independent r-variable LPs. The closed convex feasible core set gives existence and uniqueness of its squared-distance minimizer by coercivity and strict convexity. The velocity slice is compact; at a vertex its positive-support columns must be independent in the stacked constraint matrix of rank n-r+1. For codimension one, singleton zero-coefficient supports and opposite-sign pairs exhaust vertices (a pair of zero coefficients gives a nonextreme mixture). The support bound is sharp: take the first n-r+1 entries constrained equal and the rest free, with b all ones, and use the normalized constant block with all free entries zero. Both completion obstructions are independent; once both are absent the same product witness works, also for rectangular cores.
